title: Spring Data JPA Quick Revision Handbook
summary: Night-before revision notes on Spring Data JPA: entities and relationships, repositories and derived queries, @Query, pagination and sorting, @Transactional, lazy vs eager loading, and the N+1 problem.

chapters.title: Entities and Relationships
points: Entity mental model: @Entity class maps to a table, @Id marks the primary key, @GeneratedValue(strategy = IDENTITY) lets the DB assign it, and a no-arg constructor is required
@OneToMany(mappedBy = "order") is the inverse side; the @ManyToOne side with @JoinColumn owns the foreign key and is the one that writes it
@ManyToMany needs a @JoinTable; for extra columns on the link, model an explicit join entity with two @ManyToOne instead
cascade = CascadeType.ALL plus orphanRemoval = true makes children follow the parent's save and delete; use it only for owned children
Keep both sides in sync with helper methods like order.addItem(item); setting only the inverse side persists nothing

chapters.title: Repositories and Derived Queries
points: JpaRepository<T, ID> extends CrudRepository and PagingAndSortingRepository; declare an interface and Spring generates the implementation at startup
Core methods: save (insert or merge), findById returns Optional, findAll, deleteById, existsById, count
Derived queries parse the method name: findByEmailAndActiveTrue, findByAgeGreaterThan, findByNameContainingIgnoreCase, findTop3ByOrderByCreatedAtDesc
Return types: Optional<T> for at most one, List<T> for many, plus existsBy, countBy and deleteBy prefixes
A property name that does not exist in the entity fails at startup with a PropertyReferenceException, not at call time

chapters.title: @Query, Pagination and Sorting
points: @Query("select u from User u where u.email = :email") takes JPQL on entities and fields, not table and column names; bind with @Param
nativeQuery = true runs raw SQL; use it for DB-specific features, and expect no automatic entity-name translation
@Modifying with @Query runs update or delete statements; add clearAutomatically = true so the persistence context is not stale
Pageable parameter with PageRequest.of(page, size, Sort.by("createdAt").descending()); pages are zero-indexed
Page<T> runs an extra count query and exposes total elements and pages; Slice<T> skips the count and only knows whether a next page exists

chapters.title: Transactions with @Transactional
points: @Transactional wraps a method in a transaction through a proxy: commit on success, rollback on a RuntimeException or Error
Checked exceptions do not roll back by default; add rollbackFor = Exception.class to change that
Self-invocation bypasses the proxy: a this.method() call to another @Transactional method in the same class starts no transaction
Put it on the service layer, not the repository or controller; readOnly = true on read paths skips dirty checking and signals intent
Propagation REQUIRED (default) joins the existing transaction; REQUIRES_NEW suspends it and starts an independent one

chapters.title: Lazy vs Eager Loading and the N+1 Problem
points: Defaults: @ManyToOne and @OneToOne are EAGER; @OneToMany and @ManyToMany are LAZY, and the safe habit is to set fetch = LAZY on everything
Lazy associations are proxies loaded on first access; touching one after the transaction closes throws LazyInitializationException
N+1 problem: one query loads N parents, then looping over a lazy child collection fires N more queries, one per parent
Fix with join fetch in @Query (select o from Order o join fetch o.items) or @EntityGraph(attributePaths = "items") on the repository method
Also fix with @BatchSize or default_batch_fetch_size to load children in IN batches; never fix it by switching to EAGER; join fetch on a collection with Pageable paginates in memory

chapters.title: Spring Data JPA Cheat Sheet
points: Annotations: @Entity @Id @GeneratedValue @OneToMany(mappedBy) @ManyToOne @JoinColumn @Query @Param @Modifying @Transactional @EntityGraph
Derived keywords: findBy, existsBy, countBy, deleteBy, And, Or, Between, In, Containing, OrderBy, Top3
Paging: PageRequest.of(page, size, sort) with Page for totals and Slice for a cheaper next check
Transactions: service layer, rollback on RuntimeException only, avoid self-invocation, readOnly for reads
Performance: set LAZY everywhere, fix N+1 with join fetch, EntityGraph or BatchSize, and turn on spring.jpa.show-sql to spot it
